newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia says self-sufficient in food in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia says self-sufficient in food in 1996/97.

text.p: Ethiopia said on Thursday it was self-sufficient in food with a bumper harvest of some 11.7 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (September to February) crop year.

"Crop production during the 1996/97 season is over 11.7 million tonnes...which far exceeds the estimated 8.7 million tonnes required to feed the country's 55 million population during the period," Agriculture Minister Teketel Forsido said.
He added some three million tonnes would be surplus. The minister did not give details of the crop but Ethiopia grows mainly cereals.
Ethiopian agriculture has steadily increased production since the overthrow of Marxist dicator Mengistu Haile Marian in 1991 and the introduction of economic reforms the following year.
Ethiopia produced 8.7 million tonnes of food in 1995/96, 7.7 million tonnes in 1994/95, 7.15 in 1993/94 and 6.9 million in 1992/93, according to a U.N. report.
Teketel said the bumper harvest was the result of good agricultural policies, rains, changes in peasant farming, a coordinated supply of inputs such as fertilisers and seeds and expert advice.
A loan scheme for peasant farmers allowed them to buy oxen to plough, he added.
But some areas of Ethiopia hit by drought have appealed for food aid this year. The country was hit by a catastrophic famine in 1984.
